questions.question: Chetan alone can do a work in 6 days working 5 hours a day. Rashmi alone can do the same work in 2 days working 10 hours a day. How many hours do they need to work together in a day to complete the same work in 4 days?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Chetan's work = 6 days × 5 hours/day = 30 hours

Rashmi's work = 2 days × 10 hours/day = 20 hours

**Calculations:**

1. Work done per hour:

⇒ Chetan's work rate = 1 work unit / 30 hours = 1/30 work units/hour

⇒ Rashmi's work rate = 1 work unit / 20 hours = 1/20 work units/hour

2. Combined work rate:

⇒ Combined work rate = (1/30) + (1/20)

Finding a common denominator (LCM of 30 and 20 is 60):

⇒ Combined work rate = (2/60) + (3/60) = 5/60 = 1/12 work units/hour

3. Total work to be done in 4 days:

⇒ Total hours in 4 days = 4 days × x hours/day

4. Total work done in 4 days:

⇒ Total work = Combined work rate × Total hours

⇒ 1 = (1/12) × (4x)

5. Solving for x:

⇒ 1 = 4x / 12

⇒ 1 = x / 3

⇒ x = 3 hours

**∴ Chetan and Rashmi need to work together for 3 hours a day to complete the work in 4 days.**

questions.question: Two trains of lengths 80 m and 100 m are moving in the same direction with their speeds in the ratio of 3 ∶ 2 respectively. If they cross a 20 m long bridge, then find the ratio of the time taken by first train to the time taken by second train to cross the bridge?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

**Time Ratio** = (Distance₁ / Speed₁) : (Distance₂ / Speed₂)

Distance₁ = 80 + 20 = 100 m; Distance₂ = 100 + 20 = 120 m

Speed ratio = 3 : 2 ⇒ Ratio = (100 / 3) : (120 / 2) = (100 / 3) : 60

Simplified Ratio = 100 : 180 = 5 : 9

**∴ The correct answer is 5 : 9.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Length of **Train 1** (L₁) = 80 m, Length of **Train 2** (L₂) = 100 m

Length of **Bridge** (Lb) = 20 m

Ratio of Speeds (S₁ : S₂) = 3 : 2

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e9365bb5076ddee8daec93ba246ab00447d0571a44bfc60af13d98e940a7a49e.png] 

**Formula Used:**

Time = Total Distance ÷ Speed

Total Distance = Length of Train + Length of Bridge

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let Speeds be S₁ = 3x and S₂ = 2x

⇒ Total Distance for Train 1 (D₁) = 80 + 20 = 100 m

⇒ Total Distance for Train 2 (D₂) = 100 + 20 = 120 m

⇒ Time taken by Train 1 (T₁) = 100 / 3x

⇒ Time taken by Train 2 (T₂) = 120 / 2x = 60 / x

⇒ Ratio T₁ : T₂ = (100 / 3x) : (60 / x)

⇒ Ratio = (100 / 3) : 60 = 100 : 180

⇒ Ratio = 5 : 9

**∴ The correct answer is 5 : 9.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Crossing Stationary Objects

When a train crosses a bridge, platform, or another stationary train, the total distance covered is the sum of the lengths of the train and the object.

Relative Speed

If two objects move in the same direction, relative speed = S₁ − S₂. If they move in opposite directions, relative speed = S₁ + S₂.

Unit Conversion

To convert km/h to m/s, multiply by 5/18. To convert m/s to km/h, multiply by 18/5.</p

questions.question: A policeman chases a thief on a straight road. The policeman catches the thief in 15 minutes if he drives with a speed of 60 km/h and catches the thief in 0.5 hours if he drives with a speed 45 km/h. What should be his driving speed (in km/h) to catch the thief in just 10 minutes?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of **Time** taken to catch: T₁ : T₂ = 15 : 30 = 1 : 2.

Ratio of **Relative Speed** (Vₚ − Vₜ): R₁ : R₂ = 2 : 1 (inverse ratio).

⇒ (60 − Vₜ) = 2 × (45 − Vₜ) ⇒ 60 − Vₜ = 90 − 2Vₜ ⇒ **Vₜ = 30 km/h**.

Relative speed for 15 min = 60 − 30 = 30 km/h. For 10 min, required relative speed = (30 × 15) ÷ 10 = 45 km/h.

Required Speed of **Policeman** = 45 + 30 = 75 km/h.

**∴ The correct answer is 75 km/h.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Case 1: **Policeman speed** (Vₚ₁) = 60 km/h, Time (T₁) = 15 min = 0.25 hr.

Case 2: **Policeman speed** (Vₚ₂) = 45 km/h, Time (T₂) = 0.5 hr.

**Formula Used:**

Relative Speed (same direction) = Vₚ − Vₜ

Initial Distance (D) = (Vₚ − Vₜ) × Time

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f56bf5ca06ba0bd56d88188c716f9355a741f3c7ded05ca5d16a569db2b11af5.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let Vₜ be the speed of the **thief** and **x** be the initial distance.

⇒ x = (60 − Vₜ) × 0.25 --- (Eq 1)

⇒ x = (45 − Vₜ) × 0.5 --- (Eq 2)

⇒ (60 − Vₜ) × 0.25 = (45 − Vₜ) × 0.5

⇒ 60 − Vₜ = 2(45 − Vₜ) ⇒ 60 − Vₜ = 90 − 2Vₜ

⇒ **Vₜ = 30 km/h**

⇒ Initial distance x = (60 − 30) × 0.25 = 30 × 0.25 = **7.5 km**

⇒ Required time (T₃) = 10 min = 10/60 = 1/6 hr

⇒ 7.5 = (Vₚ₃ − 30) × (1/6)

⇒ 7.5 × 6 = Vₚ₃ − 30 ⇒ 45 = Vₚ₃ − 30

⇒ **Vₚ₃ = 75 km/h**

**∴ The correct answer is 75 km/h.**

**__Additional Information__**

Relative Speed Concept

When two objects move in the same direction, the relative speed is the difference of their speeds: Vᵣₑₗ = V₁ − V₂.

Catching Time Formula

Time to catch = (Initial distance between objects) ÷ (Relative speed of the objects).

Speed-Time Relation

For a constant distance, speed is inversely proportional to time: S₁/S₂ = T₂/T₁.</p

questions.question: The average weight of 56 students in a group is 55 kg. If 12 students of average weight 60 kg leave and 6 students of average weight 52.5 kg join the group, then the average weight of the remaining students in the group decreased by:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Net deviation from the original **average weight** (55 kg) is calculated as follows:

Loss due to 12 students (60 kg) leaving: 12 × (60 − 55) = 60 kg

Loss due to 6 students (52.5 kg) joining: 6 × (55 − 52.5) = 15 kg

Total net weight loss = 60 + 15 = 75 kg

Total remaining students = 56 − 12 + 6 = 50 students

Average decrease = Total net weight loss ÷ Total students = 75 ÷ 50 = 1.5 kg

**∴ The correct answer is 1.5 kg.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Initial students = 56, Initial Average = 55 kg. Students left = 12 (Avg 60 kg), Students joined = 6 (Avg 52.5 kg).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b09bd21d4c77329947ce7b36f0f8c4f26f00840b1da367ff21949b7a55f5c654.png] 

Total initial weight = 56 × 55 = 3080 kg

Weight of 12 students who left = 12 × 60 = 720 kg

Weight of 6 students who joined = 6 × 52.5 = 315 kg

⇒ New total weight = 3080 − 720 + 315 = 2675 kg

⇒ Total remaining students = 56 − 12 + 6 = 50 students

⇒ New average weight = 2675 ÷ 50 = 53.5 kg

⇒ Decrease in average weight = 55 − 53.5 = 1.5 kg

**∴ The correct answer is 1.5 kg.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Average weight formula

Average = (Sum of all observations) ÷ (Total number of observations)

Net Deviation Method

Change in Average = (Net change in sum) ÷ (New total number of items). This avoids calculating large products.

Impact of Inclusion/Exclusion

If the weight of the joining person is more than the average, the average increases; if less, the average decreases.</p

Efficiency of A = 15 ÷ 3 = 5 units/hr, B = 15 ÷ 5 = 3 units/hr.

A works alone from 7 am to 8 am → Fills 5 units, remaining = 15 − 5 = 10 units.

Both A and B working together take = 10 ÷ (5 + 3) = 10/8 = 1 hour 15 minutes.

Time when the tank is filled = 8:00 am + 1 hour 15 minutes = 9 : 15 am.

**∴ The correct answer is 9 : 15 am.**

questions.question: The average speed of Gaurav during a two-way journey is 15 km/h. If he walked a distance of 20 km every hour while going, then his speed while returning will be:
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

**Average Speed** for equal distance (two-way) = 2xy ÷ (x + y)

Given: **Average Speed** = 15 km/h, **Going Speed** (x) = 20 km/h

15 = (2 × 20 × y) ÷ (20 + y)

15 × (20 + y) = 40y ⇒ 300 + 15y = 40y ⇒ 25y = 300 ⇒ y = 12 km/h

**∴ The correct answer is 12 km/h.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Going Speed** (v₁) = 20 km/h (since he walks 20 km every hour)

**Average Speed** (Vₐvg) = 15 km/h

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e92cedad65df74a2f5aa13b7dd64bdaaac10d59bc476eaa3e02cfe29f6017aff.png] 

**Formula Used:**

Average Speed = **Total Distance** ÷ **Total Time**

For two equal distances: Vₐvg = 2v₁v₂ ÷ (v₁ + v₂)

**Calculations:**

⇒ 15 = (2 × 20 × v₂) ÷ (20 + v₂)

⇒ 15 × (20 + v₂) = 40v₂

⇒ 300 + 15v₂ = 40v₂

⇒ 40v₂ − 15v₂ = 300

⇒ 25v₂ = 300

⇒ v₂ = 300 ÷ 25

⇒ v₂ = 12 km/h

**∴ The correct answer is 12 km/h.**

**__Additional Information__**

Average Speed for Different Distances

If a person covers distances d₁, d₂ at speeds v₁, v₂, then Average Speed = (d₁ + d₂) ÷ (d₁/v₁ + d₂/v₂).

Harmonic Mean

For equal distance segments, the **average speed** is always the **Harmonic Mean** of the individual speeds.

Relative Speed

When two objects move in opposite directions, relative speed = s₁ + s₂. In the same direction, relative speed = |s₁ − s₂|.</p

questions.question: A batsman has a definite average for 11 innings. That batsman scores 120 runs in his 12th innings due to which his average increased by 5 runs. Accordingly, what is the average of the batsman after 12 innings?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

To find the **new average** after an increase: **New Average** = Score in last innings − (Previous number of innings × Increase in average)

New Average = 120 − (11 × 5)

New Average = 120 − 55 = 65

**∴ The correct answer is 65.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Number of initial innings = 11

Runs in 12th inning = 120

Increase in average = 5

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b7f27fd214c101d52e690ed8b8dd19cadc817f3f342238ba5a308c71fa1aa3e4.png] 

Let the **average** of the first 11 innings be x.

Total runs in 11 innings = 11x

Total runs in 12 innings = 11x + 120

According to the problem, the **new average** is (x + 5).

⇒ Total runs in 12 innings = 12 × (x + 5)

⇒ 11x + 120 = 12x + 60

⇒ 12x − 11x = 120 − 60

⇒ x = 60

⇒ New average after 12 innings = x + 5 = 60 + 5 = 65

**∴ The correct answer is 65.**

**__Additional Information__**

Batting Average Formula

Batting Average = Total Runs Scored ÷ Total Number of Innings (or times out).

Net Change in Average

If the average of n items is A, and a new item x is added such that the new average is (A + k), then x = A + k × (n + 1).

Bowling Average

Bowling Average = Total Runs Conceded ÷ Total Wickets Taken. A lower bowling average is considered better performance.

Sum of Observations

questions.question: If x+(1)/(3x)=5, then the value of 27x³+(1)/(x³) will be:
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Multiply the given equation by 3: **3x + 1/x = 15**.

Use the direct shortcut: If **a + b = k**, then **a³ + b³ = k³ − 3abk**.

Here, **a = 3x**, **b = 1/x**, so **ab = 3** and **k = 15**.

Value = 15³ − 3 × 3 × 15 = 3375 − 135 = 3240.

**∴ The correct answer is 3240.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** x + 1/(3x) = 5

**Formula Used:** (a + b)³ = a³ + b³ + 3ab(a + b)

⇒ Multiply the given equation by 3 on both sides:

⇒ 3 × (x + 1/(3x)) = 3 × 5

⇒ 3x + 1/x = 15

⇒ **Cubing both sides** of the equation:

⇒ (3x + 1/x)³ = 15³

⇒ (3x)³ + (1/x)³ + 3 × 3x × (1/x) × (3x + 1/x) = 3375

⇒ 27x³ + 1/x³ + 9 × (3x + 1/x) = 3375

⇒ Substitute (3x + 1/x) = 15:

⇒ 27x³ + 1/x³ + 9 × 15 = 3375

⇒ 27x³ + 1/x³ + 135 = 3375

⇒ 27x³ + 1/x³ = 3375 − 135 = 3240

**∴ The correct answer is 3240.**

**__Additional Information__**

Algebraic Cube Identity

The basic identity for the cube of a sum is (a + b)³ = a³ + b³ + 3ab(a + b). It is frequently used to find the sum of cubes when the sum and product of two terms are known.

Reciprocal Power Shortcut

If x + 1/x = k, then x³ + 1/x³ = k³ − 3k. This can be extended to coefficients: if ax + b/x = k, then (ax)³ + (b/x)³ = k³ − 3(ab)k.

Successive Calculation

To find higher powers like x⁶, first find the square (x² + 1/x²) and then cube that result, or vice versa.</p

questions.question: The ratio of the incomes of A and B in 2020 was 5 ∶ 4. The ratios of their individual incomes in 2020 and 2021 were 4 ∶ 5 and 2 ∶ 3, respectively. If the total income A and B in 2021 was Rs.7,05,600, then what was the income (in Rs.) of B in 2021?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Income A : B (2020) = 5 : 4

Change ratios: A (4 : 5) → A (2021) = 5 × (5 ÷ 4) = 6.25 units

Change ratios: B (2 : 3) → B (2021) = 4 × (3 ÷ 2) = 6 units

Income A : B (2021) = 6.25 : 6 = 25 : 24 (Total = 49 units)

B's 2021 income = (24 ÷ 49) × 7,05,600 = 24 × 14,400 = Rs. 3,45,600

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 3,45,600.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Income ratio A : B (2020) = 5 : 4

Individual income ratio A (2020 : 2021) = 4 : 5

Individual income ratio B (2020 : 2021) = 2 : 3

Total income of A and B in 2021 = Rs. 7,05,600

**Formula Used:**

New Income = Old Income × (New Ratio Part ÷ Old Ratio Part)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/6ac8786cc91cf5fb55af3185917595579be532ce41d699afccc5d9693591e1a4.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ To make the 2020 income of A (5) divisible by 4 and B (4) divisible by 2, multiply the A:B (2020) ratio by 4.

⇒ New A:B (2020) = (5 × 4) : (4 × 4) = 20 : 16

⇒ A's income in 2021 = (20 ÷ 4) × 5 = 25 units

⇒ B's income in 2021 = (16 ÷ 2) × 3 = 24 units

⇒ Total income in 2021 = 25 + 24 = 49 units

⇒ Given 49 units = 7,05,600

⇒ 1 unit = 7,05,600 ÷ 49 = 14,400

⇒ Income of B in 2021 = 24 × 14,400 = 3,45,600

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 3,45,600.**

**__Additional Information__**

Ratio Normalization

When connecting ratios across different time frames, find a common multiple for the shared term (usually the base year value) to simplify calculations.

Compound Ratios

The final ratio of two variables after changes can be found by multiplying the initial ratio parts by their respective fractional change factors.

Division by Ratio

To find an individual part, use the formula: Share = (Individual Ratio ÷ Sum of Ratio Parts) × Total Value.</p

questions.question: In a school there are 96 teachers, out of which (3)/(8)th teaches High school classes. If (2)/(9)th of the High school teachers are Mathematics teachers. then the number of High school teachers who don't teach Mathematics are:
questions.solution:
**Given: **

Number of school teachers = 96

High school teachers = 3/8th

Mathematics teachers = 2/9th of high school teachers

**Calculation: **

Number of high school teachers = 3/8 of 96 = 36

⇒ Mathematics teacher = 2/9 of 36 = 8

⇒ Non mathematics teacher = 36 - 8 = 28

∴ The number of High school teachers who don't teach Mathematics are 28

The correct option is 3 i.e. 28

questions.question: Three friends A, B and C start running around a circular stadium and complete a single round in 24 seconds, 36 seconds and 30 seconds, respectively. After how many minutes will they meet again at the starting point ?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Time taken to meet again at the starting point = LCM of individual times taken by each person.

⇒ LCM of 24, 36 and 30 seconds = 360 seconds.

⇒ Convert time into minutes = 360 ÷ 60 = 6 minutes.

**∴ The correct answer is 6 minutes.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/605c7e51d63bb3b319e97ae9499fc776dd50c03f8ed39498ed9095035fdc426a.png] 

**Given:**

Time taken by A to complete a round = 24 seconds

Time taken by B to complete a round = 36 seconds

Time taken by C to complete a round = 30 seconds

**Formula Used:**

Time after which they meet at the starting point = LCM of individual times.

**Calculation:**

⇒ Prime factorisation of 24 = 2³ × 3

⇒ Prime factorisation of 36 = 2² × 3²

⇒ Prime factorisation of 30 = 2 × 3 × 5

⇒ LCM (24, 36, 30) = Highest powers of all prime factors = 2³ × 3² × 5

⇒ LCM = 8 × 9 × 5 = 360 seconds

⇒ We know that 1 minute = 60 seconds

⇒ Time in minutes = 360 ÷ 60 = 6 minutes

**∴ The correct answer is 6 minutes.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Meeting at the Starting Point

When multiple runners run on a circular track, the time after which they all meet simultaneously at the starting point is always the LCM of the times taken by each runner to complete one full round.

Meeting Anywhere on the Track for the First Time

If two runners start running simultaneously from the exact same point, they will meet for the first time anywhere on the track after Time = Track Length ÷ Relative Speed.

Relative Speed on a Circular Track

When moving in the same direction, relative speed = a − b. When moving in opposite directions, relative speed = a + b.

questions.question: “Blue Baby Syndrome” caused by which among the following salts presence in water?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Nitrates**.

 
• The most common cause of blue baby syndrome is **water contaminated with nitrates**.
 
• After a baby drinks formula made with nitrate-rich water, the body converts the nitrates into nitrites.
 
• It’s characterized by an overall skin color with a blue or purple tinge, called cyanosis.
 
• This bluish appearance is most noticeable where the skin is thin, such as the lips, earlobes, and nail beds. Blue baby syndrome, while not common, can occur due to several congenital (meaning present at birth) heart defects or environmental or genetic factors.
